stemMd: Two substrates have similar molecular formulae, but an enzyme catalyses a reaction of only one. Which explanation is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The unused substrate must contain no carbon.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The enzyme changes the atomic numbers of substrate atoms.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Enzymes must react equally with all molecules in solution.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The active site interacts with the substrate's particular shape and chemical groups.

explanationMd: Binding depends on three-dimensional fit and chemical interactions, not formula alone. Molecules with similar composition may arrange their atoms differently and therefore interact differently with an active site.

distractorRationale.b: Equal or similar mass does not ensure binding.
distractorRationale.c: Chemical catalysis does not alter nuclei.
distractorRationale.a: Organic substrates can both contain carbon.
